## OPERATOR RULING — criterion 11's row-12-OUTBOUND gap is to be BUILT, not amended away

Asked whether to build the missing row-12 outbound cell (rebar pushing a parent onto a DC issue) or to
amend criterion 11 and file it as a follow-up, the operator chose **BUILD IT NOW**. In progress as a
third change stacked on 1279/1280.

Rationale on the record: every "Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" defect this epic has
found — d067 (status never transitioned), 8d68 (inbound update never minted an identity), 751e
(unassign), 2b16 (inbound link removal), 88d9 (inbound parent clear) — sits in the parent/assignee/link
area, and every one was a SILENT success. Outbound parent-set is the untested corner of exactly that
area, so leaving it unproven is where the next defect of the class would hide. Parity is the operator's
stated instrument for confidence that DC ships defect-free, so a known hole in the mutation matrix is not
something to record and move past.

**One outcome is explicitly acceptable and is NOT a failure:** if the epic-parent and sub-task-parent
paths turn out to collapse into one already-covered path, the honest result is to amend the criterion
rather than add a duplicate cell. The instruction to the implementer is to establish the real contract
first — DC's `set_parent` raises `NotImplementedError` for at least some cases and that exception is
SWALLOWED at `dispatch_one.py:564`, so it must be asserted directly against the transport (the existing
row-12 EPIC cell's shape) rather than through the reconciler subprocess. A cell that passes because an
exception was swallowed is the exact vacuity this stack just removed.

Row 14 inbound's deviation is amended regardless, and that is independent of this ruling: its prescribed
oracle is provably unsatisfiable — snapshot entries carry no `jira_key` FIELD
(`_snapshot_schema.py:26,99`), so `differ.py:641-651`'s `local_entry.get("jira_key")` is always falsy and
the probe can never fire in production.
